subject: Request: Fees-at-risk & termination language for SLA exhibit
messages:
From: Jared Lowe <jared.lowe@rapidlogix.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@rapidlogix.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0400
Subject: SLA: fees-at-risk / termination language

Connor —

Thanks for sending over the master services agreement draft. Our legal/procurement team reviewed the SLA exhibit and we have two sticking points that are showstoppers for us:

1) Credits only for downtime: we need a fees-at-risk clause (we're asking for at-risk fees equal to 12 months of committed fees) if uptime falls below the agreed SLOs for more than two consecutive months.
2) Termination for convenience / fee-based termination: we need an explicit termination right with a fee payment rather than just credits — otherwise the credit-only remedy doesn't give us operational protection.

We appreciate standard vendor limits, but given this will be in production for a critical customer-facing flow, RapidLogix requires stronger economic remedies.

I'm attaching our redlines and a proposed paragraph that ties termination/fee into repeated SLA failures. Please review and let me know if Redwood can accept these as-is or propose a compromise.

Regards,
Jared Lowe
Director, Procurement
RapidLogix

Attachments: RapidLogix_Redlines_20260609.docx, SLA_Exhibit_RapidLogix_v1.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: SLA: fees-at-risk / termination language

Connor / Neha —

Legal reviewed RapidLogix's redlines. High level: we do not accept open-ended "fees at risk" equal to 12 months' revenue. That is commercially excessive and creates open exposure for Redwood that our underwriters won't permit.

Proposed counter (reasonable compromise we can present):
- Retain our standard credit regime tied to monthly SLOs (examples: 99.9% = credits up to 10% of monthly invoice; 99.0% = credits up to 30% of monthly invoice).
- Add a termination-for-material-breach right if the customer experiences two consecutive months below the 99.0% SLO and the vendor fails to cure within 30 days after notice. Termination would allow pro-rated refunds for pre-paid fees and a capped termination fee equal to three (3) months of average monthly fees (not 12 months).
- Add an escalation path: exceptions above the 3-month cap require approval by VP Sales + Legal and will be handled as a one-off commercial exception only.

If RapidLogix insists on a larger fee-at-risk, we can surface to VP Sales for sign-off, but we should try the above first.

Also note: customer asked for additional evidence (SOC2, data retention logs). Let's prepare the security packet in parallel. Rafael, please pull the SOC2 cert and any audit logs we can share under NDA.

Marissa Cole
Head of Contracts (acting)
Redwood Inference
From: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
To: Jared Lowe <jared.lowe@rapidlogix.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA: fees-at-risk / termination language

Jared — following up after Legal's review. We want to be practical and keep RapidLogix productive. Our commercial counter: the following is what we can commit to in the SLA exhibit without escalation to our executive pricing desk:

1) Retain credits-based remediation for single-month SLO misses with published credit tables.
2) For sustained underperformance (two consecutive months with monthly uptime < 99.0%), customer may:
   a) Provide notice and require Redwood to cure within 30 days. If Redwood fails to cure, RapidLogix may terminate for material breach.
   b) In case of termination under this provision, Redwood will pay a termination fee capped at three (3) months of average monthly fees (calculated over the trailing 6 months) OR refund any pre-paid unused fees.
3) Exceptions above the 3-month cap or fee-at-risk structures requested by the customer must be approved by VP Sales + Legal and will be handled as a signed addendum (one-off).

We can also provide SOC2 Type II and an operations packet on data retention and latency monitoring under NDA — I'll have Rafael drop the links.

If that aligns, can we lock the language and move to redline the exhibit? Alternatively, we can jump on a call today to resolve open points.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Connor / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick review and the proposed compromise. We appreciate Redwood being willing to add a termination-for-material-breach path and a capped termination fee. A couple of follow-ups from procurement:

1) RapidLogix will accept a capped termination fee set to three (3) months of average monthly fees as a starting point, provided the termination triggers are spelled out (two consecutive months <99.0% + 30-day cure).
2) However, on the fees-at-risk side we still want the option to escalate to your VP Sales for a higher cap in the event of high-value business impact. Can you confirm the escalation timeline and who will be the contact?
3) Please send the SOC2 Type II and the operations packet under NDA. We'll execute the redlined exhibit once legal has the updated language.

I'll book a 30-minute call for tomorrow to finalize the redline. Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
Jared Lowe
Director, Procurement
RapidLogix
